comparisons.evidence: P targets structural bottlenecks through mechanisms such as "Home-Equity-to-Habitat Swap," "Care Escrow and Family SLA," and legal-threshold avoidance. Q's strongest mechanisms, including "Personal Technical Rider" and "Grandparenting Stagecraft," improve important but generally narrower aspects of mobility, work setup, and family connection.

Q directly connects a "machine-readable specification" to property certification and proposes testing it with a spreadsheet before building infrastructure. P's "Jurisdiction Autopilot" is credible but depends on accurately representing changing multi-country rules and converting them into recommendations without crossing into unreliable legal advice.

Q's leading products can begin with lightweight manual tests, such as "20 overnight reviews" or a "manual cancellation-and-expiry calendar." P's practical ideas require legal accuracy, trusted local responders, or coordinated cross-border operations, while its wildcards explicitly require substantial "actuarial and regulatory learning."

P specifies concrete MVPs such as "location import, manual work-day classification" and rules for five jurisdiction pairs. Q is similarly specific, proposing a spreadsheet-based rider for 20 users and defined measurements such as setup time, unresolved problems, and first-week work output.

P reframes care insecurity as uncertain availability rather than merely affordability and converts housing wealth into "spatial optionality." Q comparably reframes time-zone difference as purchasable working-day "inventory" and distance from grandchildren as a storytelling mechanism rather than only a communication problem.

P spans legal-threshold avoidance, portable business administration, health recovery, family crisis governance, mission-based work, risk-triggered relocation, care capacity, and housing-asset conversion. Q spans several distinct regions—environment compatibility, asynchronous expert work, family play, continuity, and commitment decay—but covers fewer major financial, healthcare, legal, and housing mechanisms.

Q subjects survivors to explicit falsification tests such as "kill the idea if clarification cycles erase the time-zone advantage" and finishes with four sharply differentiated recommendations. P distinguishes practical ideas from wildcards, but still devotes substantial attention to mechanisms it concedes may require years of regulatory, provider, or actuarial development.
